memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites. After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, the Israelites captured its surrounding settlements and drove out the Amorites who were there. Then they turned and went up along the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army marched out to meet them in battle at Edrei. - Num 21:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Barely had Israel settled from one victory when another challenge rose up. Og, the king of Bashan, marched out with his whole army. Og was famously formidable, a giant of a man ruling a land of fortified cities. Here was a fresh test right after the last one.

Life often works this way. We overcome one difficulty only to find another waiting. There is a temptation, after a hard-won victory, to expect smooth roads ahead. Yet the wilderness rarely offers long rest. New giants appear, and old fears can return.

But notice how Israel had grown. The people who once trembled at giants and refused to enter the land are now marching forward in faith. The same God who gave them Sihon would give them Og. Past victories had taught them to trust God for the next battle.

This is how faith matures. Each remembered deliverance becomes fuel for facing the next challenge. When a new giant looms in your life, look back at what God has already done. The Lord who carried you through before will carry you through again. In Christ you are more than a conqueror, whatever stands before you (Rom 8:37).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond when a new challenge follows an old one?
2. What past victories can strengthen you for the battle you face now?
3. Where is God calling you to march forward in faith rather than fear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when new giants rise up before me, remind me of all You have already done. Give me courage to face what is ahead, trusting that in Christ I am more than a conqueror. Amen.
